class Advection2D(eqx.Module):
    """2-D advection operator.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : CartesianGrid2D
        The underlying 2-D grid.
    mask : Mask2D or None, optional
        Optional land/ocean mask; every method is then land-safe.  The
        ``(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)`` adaptive stencil hierarchies for both
        directions are pre-built once in ``__init__`` and reused on
        every call — this is the main reason the API moved from a
        per-call keyword to a class field.  Dry inputs are zeroed with
        ``jnp.where`` (so ``NaN`` on land cannot leak); the
        upwind-biased methods (everything but ``naive``) go through
        ``upwind_flux`` with the stored hierarchy narrowed to the
        method's stencil sizes, so no chosen stencil reads a dry cell;
        the face fluxes on dry faces (``mask.u`` / ``mask.v`` false) are
        zeroed before the divergence, as in :class:`Diffusion2D`, so no
        mass crosses the coast; and dry T-cells are exactly zero.
        ``None`` (default) matches the unmasked behaviour bit for bit.
    """

    grid: CartesianGrid2D
    mask: Mask2D | None
    recon: Reconstruction2D
    _mask_hierarchy_x: dict[int, Bool[Array, "Ny Nx"]] | None
    _mask_hierarchy_y: dict[int, Bool[Array, "Ny Nx"]] | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        grid: CartesianGrid2D,
        mask: Mask2D | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.grid = grid
        self.mask = mask
        self.recon = Reconstruction2D(grid=grid)
        if mask is not None:
            self._mask_hierarchy_x = mask.get_adaptive_masks(
                direction="x", stencil_sizes=_HIERARCHY_SIZES
            )
            self._mask_hierarchy_y = mask.get_adaptive_masks(
                direction="y", stencil_sizes=_HIERARCHY_SIZES
            )
        else:
            self._mask_hierarchy_x = None
            self._mask_hierarchy_y = None

    def __call__(
        self,
        h: Float[Array, "Ny Nx"],
        u: Float[Array, "Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "Ny Nx"],
        method: str = "upwind1",
        wall: str = "closed",
    ) -> Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]:
        """Advective tendency -div(h * u_vec) at T-points.

        dh[j, i] = -( (fe[j, i+1/2] - fe[j, i-1/2]) / dx
                    + (fn[j+1/2, i] - fn[j-1/2, i]) / dy )

        Parameters
        ----------
        h : Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
            Scalar at T-points.
        u : Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.
        method : str
            Reconstruction method: ``'naive'``, ``'upwind1'``, ``'upwind2'``,
            ``'upwind3'``, ``'weno3'``, ``'weno5'``, ``'weno7'``, ``'weno9'``,
            ``'wenoz5'``, or a flux-limiter TVD scheme: ``'minmod'``,
            ``'van_leer'``, ``'superbee'``, ``'mc'``.
        wall : {"closed", "open"}, default "closed"
            Lateral-boundary treatment.  ``"closed"`` (default, unchanged)
            writes the tendency only on the strict interior ``[2:-2, 2:-2]``
            and treats all four domain walls as no-flux.  ``"open"`` writes
            the full interior ``[1:-1, 1:-1]`` and computes the four
            domain-wall face fluxes with a first-order upwind reconstruction
            that reads the ghost ring, so Dirichlet / outflow / periodic
            lateral boundaries (applied by the caller to the ghost cells
            beforehand) drive horizontal transport.  Interior faces keep the
            requested high-order ``method`` and the flux field stays
            single-valued, so mass is conserved exactly.  ``"open"`` is not
            supported together with a ``mask``.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
            Advective tendency at T-points.
        """
        _validate_wall(wall, self.mask)
        if self.mask is not None:
            # Zero the dry inputs before any stencil reads them, so land
            # values (even NaN) reach neither the output nor its gradient.
            h = jnp.where(self.mask.h, h, 0.0)  # [Ny, Nx]
            u = jnp.where(self.mask.u, u, 0.0)  # [Ny, Nx]
            v = jnp.where(self.mask.v, v, 0.0)  # [Ny, Nx]
        # ── masked path: route through upwind_flux with pre-built hier. ──
        mh_x = self._mask_hierarchy_x
        mh_y = self._mask_hierarchy_y
        if mh_x is not None and mh_y is not None and method in _MASK_DISPATCHABLE:
            rfx, rfy, sizes = _rec_funcs_for_method_2d(self.recon, method)
            mask_x = narrow_mask_hierarchy(mh_x, sizes)
            mask_y = narrow_mask_hierarchy(mh_y, sizes)
            fe = upwind_flux(h, u, dim=1, rec_funcs=rfx, mask_hierarchy=mask_x)
            fn = upwind_flux(h, v, dim=0, rec_funcs=rfy, mask_hierarchy=mask_y)
        # ── unmasked path: existing dispatch ────────────────────────────
        elif method == "naive":
            fe = self.recon.naive_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.naive_y(h, v)
        elif method == "upwind1":
            fe = self.recon.upwind1_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.upwind1_y(h, v)
        elif method == "upwind2":
            fe = self.recon.upwind2_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.upwind2_y(h, v)
        elif method == "upwind3":
            fe = self.recon.upwind3_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.upwind3_y(h, v)
        elif method == "weno3":
            fe = self.recon.weno3_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.weno3_y(h, v)
        elif method == "weno5":
            fe = self.recon.weno5_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.weno5_y(h, v)
        elif method == "wenoz5":
            fe = self.recon.wenoz5_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.wenoz5_y(h, v)
        elif method == "weno7":
            fe = self.recon.weno7_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.weno7_y(h, v)
        elif method == "weno9":
            fe = self.recon.weno9_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.weno9_y(h, v)
        elif method in _TVD_LIMITERS:
            fe = self.recon.tvd_x(h, u, limiter=method)
            fn = self.recon.tvd_y(h, v, limiter=method)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown method: {method!r}")
        if self.mask is not None:
            # No flux through a dry face: fe[j, i+1/2] = 0 unless h[j, i] and
            # h[j, i+1] are both wet (mask.u), fn[j+1/2, i] likewise with
            # mask.v — the Diffusion2D face-flux masking.
            fe = jnp.where(self.mask.u, fe, 0.0)  # [Ny, Nx]
            fn = jnp.where(self.mask.v, fn, 0.0)  # [Ny, Nx]

        # dh[j, i] = -( (fe[j, i+1/2] - fe[j, i-1/2])/dx
        #             + (fn[j+1/2, i] - fn[j-1/2, i])/dy )
        # fe[j,i] is flux at east face of cell [j,i], fn[j,i] is flux at north face
        # For cell [j,i], we need fe[j,i] (east) and fe[j,i-1] (west),
        #                      and fn[j,i] (north) and fn[j-1,i] (south)
        if wall == "open":
            # Overwrite the west/east (fe cols 0, -2) and south/north
            # (fn rows 0, -2) domain-wall faces with a first-order upwind
            # flux that reads the ghost ring, then write the full interior.
            fe = fe.at[:, 0].set(_wall_upwind_flux(u[:, 0], h[:, 0], h[:, 1]))
            fe = fe.at[:, -2].set(_wall_upwind_flux(u[:, -2], h[:, -2], h[:, -1]))
            fn = fn.at[0, :].set(_wall_upwind_flux(v[0, :], h[0, :], h[1, :]))
            fn = fn.at[-2, :].set(_wall_upwind_flux(v[-2, :], h[-2, :], h[-1, :]))
            out = jnp.zeros_like(h)
            out = out.at[1:-1, 1:-1].set(
                -(
                    (fe[1:-1, 1:-1] - fe[1:-1, 0:-2]) / self.grid.dx
                    + (fn[1:-1, 1:-1] - fn[0:-2, 1:-1]) / self.grid.dy
                )
            )
        else:
            # Only use face fluxes defined by the reconstruction scheme,
            # avoiding ghost-ring flux entries.
            out = interior(
                -(
                    (fe[2:-2, 2:-2] - fe[2:-2, 1:-3]) / self.grid.dx
                    + (fn[2:-2, 2:-2] - fn[1:-3, 2:-2]) / self.grid.dy
                ),
                h,
                ghost=2,
            )
        if self.mask is not None:
            out = jnp.where(self.mask.h, out, 0.0)
        return out

        fe = jnp.where(self.mask.u, fe, 0.0)  # [Ny, Nx]
        fn = jnp.where(self.mask.v, fn, 0.0)  # [Ny, Nx]

    # dh[j, i] = -( (fe[j, i+1/2] - fe[j, i-1/2])/dx
    #             + (fn[j+1/2, i] - fn[j-1/2, i])/dy )
    # fe[j,i] is flux at east face of cell [j,i], fn[j,i] is flux at north face
    # For cell [j,i], we need fe[j,i] (east) and fe[j,i-1] (west),
    #                      and fn[j,i] (north) and fn[j-1,i] (south)
    if wall == "open":
        # Overwrite the west/east (fe cols 0, -2) and south/north
        # (fn rows 0, -2) domain-wall faces with a first-order upwind
        # flux that reads the ghost ring, then write the full interior.
        fe = fe.at[:, 0].set(_wall_upwind_flux(u[:, 0], h[:, 0], h[:, 1]))
        fe = fe.at[:, -2].set(_wall_upwind_flux(u[:, -2], h[:, -2], h[:, -1]))
        fn = fn.at[0, :].set(_wall_upwind_flux(v[0, :], h[0, :], h[1, :]))
        fn = fn.at[-2, :].set(_wall_upwind_flux(v[-2, :], h[-2, :], h[-1, :]))
        out = jnp.zeros_like(h)
        out = out.at[1:-1, 1:-1].set(
            -(
                (fe[1:-1, 1:-1] - fe[1:-1, 0:-2]) / self.grid.dx
                + (fn[1:-1, 1:-1] - fn[0:-2, 1:-1]) / self.grid.dy
            )
        )
    else:
        # Only use face fluxes defined by the reconstruction scheme,
        # avoiding ghost-ring flux entries.
        out = interior(
            -(
                (fe[2:-2, 2:-2] - fe[2:-2, 1:-3]) / self.grid.dx
                + (fn[2:-2, 2:-2] - fn[1:-3, 2:-2]) / self.grid.dy
            ),
            h,
            ghost=2,
        )
    if self.mask is not None:
        out = jnp.where(self.mask.h, out, 0.0)
    return out

As in :class:Advection2D, dry inputs are zeroed with jnp.where, the upwind-biased methods go through upwind_flux with the stored 3-D hierarchies narrowed to the method's stencil sizes — the z axis is treated as a batch dimension throughout — and the face fluxes on dry faces (mask.u / mask.v false) are zeroed before the divergence.

Pivoted from Mask2D to Mask3D per issue #209 Q4 for type-uniformity with the rest of the 3-D operator suite. A vertically-homogeneous 3-D mask (the 2-D mask broadcast over z) reproduces the old 2-D-mask-broadcast behaviour. A genuinely vertically-varying mask is now natively supported.

class Advection3D(eqx.Module):
    """3-D advection operator (horizontal plane per z-level).

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : CartesianGrid3D
        The underlying 3-D grid.
    mask : Mask3D or None, optional
        Optional 3-D land/ocean mask; every method is then land-safe.
        Pre-builds native 3-D adaptive stencil hierarchies
        ``(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)`` in both horizontal directions in
        ``__init__``.  As in :class:`Advection2D`, dry inputs are zeroed
        with ``jnp.where``, the upwind-biased methods go through
        ``upwind_flux`` with the stored 3-D hierarchies narrowed to the
        method's stencil sizes — the z axis is treated as a batch
        dimension throughout — and the face fluxes on dry faces
        (``mask.u`` / ``mask.v`` false) are zeroed before the divergence.

        Pivoted from ``Mask2D`` to ``Mask3D`` per issue #209 Q4 for
        type-uniformity with the rest of the 3-D operator suite.  A
        vertically-homogeneous 3-D mask (the 2-D mask broadcast over
        z) reproduces the old 2-D-mask-broadcast behaviour.  A
        genuinely vertically-varying mask is now natively supported.
    """

    grid: CartesianGrid3D
    mask: Mask3D | None
    recon: Reconstruction3D
    _mask_hierarchy_x: dict[int, Bool[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]] | None
    _mask_hierarchy_y: dict[int, Bool[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]] | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        grid: CartesianGrid3D,
        mask: Mask3D | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.grid = grid
        self.mask = mask
        self.recon = Reconstruction3D(grid=grid)
        if mask is not None:
            self._mask_hierarchy_x = mask.get_adaptive_masks(
                direction="x", stencil_sizes=_HIERARCHY_SIZES
            )
            self._mask_hierarchy_y = mask.get_adaptive_masks(
                direction="y", stencil_sizes=_HIERARCHY_SIZES
            )
        else:
            self._mask_hierarchy_x = None
            self._mask_hierarchy_y = None

    def __call__(
        self,
        h: Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"],
        u: Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"],
        method: str = "upwind1",
        wall: str = "closed",
    ) -> Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]:
        """Advective tendency -div(h * u_vec) at T-points over all z-levels.

        Parameters
        ----------
        h : Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
            Scalar at T-points.
        u : Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.
        method : str
            Reconstruction method: ``'naive'``, ``'upwind1'``, ``'weno3'``,
            ``'weno5'``, ``'wenoz5'``, ``'weno7'``, ``'weno9'``, or a
            flux-limiter TVD scheme: ``'minmod'``, ``'van_leer'``,
            ``'superbee'``, ``'mc'``.  (``upwind2`` / ``upwind3`` are 1-D /
            2-D only: :class:`Reconstruction3D` has no such stencils.)
        wall : {"closed", "open"}, default "closed"
            Lateral-boundary treatment for the horizontal plane.
            ``"closed"`` (default, unchanged) writes the horizontal tendency
            only on the strict interior ``[1:-1, 2:-2, 2:-2]`` and treats the
            four lateral walls as no-flux — the wall-adjacent interior ring
            holds stale values.  ``"open"`` writes the full interior
            ``[1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1]`` and computes the lateral domain-wall face
            fluxes with a first-order upwind reconstruction that reads the
            ghost ring, so Dirichlet / outflow / periodic lateral boundaries
            (applied by the caller to the ghost cells beforehand) drive
            horizontal transport.  Interior faces keep the requested
            high-order ``method`` and the flux field stays single-valued, so
            mass is conserved exactly.  The z axis is a batch dimension and is
            unaffected.  ``"open"`` is not supported together with a ``mask``.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
            Advective tendency at T-points.
        """
        _validate_wall(wall, self.mask)
        if self.mask is not None:
            # Zero the dry inputs before any stencil reads them, so land
            # values (even NaN) reach neither the output nor its gradient.
            h = jnp.where(self.mask.h, h, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]
            u = jnp.where(self.mask.u, u, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]
            v = jnp.where(self.mask.v, v, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]
        # ── masked path: route through upwind_flux with pre-built 3-D hier. ──
        mh_x = self._mask_hierarchy_x
        mh_y = self._mask_hierarchy_y
        if mh_x is not None and mh_y is not None and method in _MASK_DISPATCHABLE:
            rfx, rfy, sizes = _rec_funcs_for_method_3d(self.recon, method)
            mask_x = narrow_mask_hierarchy(mh_x, sizes)
            mask_y = narrow_mask_hierarchy(mh_y, sizes)
            # 3-D arrays: x-flux axis is 2, y-flux axis is 1.
            fe = upwind_flux(h, u, dim=2, rec_funcs=rfx, mask_hierarchy=mask_x)
            fn = upwind_flux(h, v, dim=1, rec_funcs=rfy, mask_hierarchy=mask_y)
        # ── unmasked path: existing dispatch ────────────────────────────
        elif method == "naive":
            fe = self.recon.naive_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.naive_y(h, v)
        elif method == "upwind1":
            fe = self.recon.upwind1_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.upwind1_y(h, v)
        elif method == "weno3":
            fe = self.recon.weno3_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.weno3_y(h, v)
        elif method == "weno5":
            fe = self.recon.weno5_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.weno5_y(h, v)
        elif method == "wenoz5":
            fe = self.recon.wenoz5_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.wenoz5_y(h, v)
        elif method == "weno7":
            fe = self.recon.weno7_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.weno7_y(h, v)
        elif method == "weno9":
            fe = self.recon.weno9_x(h, u)
            fn = self.recon.weno9_y(h, v)
        elif method in _TVD_LIMITERS:
            fe = self.recon.tvd_x(h, u, limiter=method)
            fn = self.recon.tvd_y(h, v, limiter=method)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown method: {method!r}")
        if self.mask is not None:
            # No flux through a dry face (mask.u / mask.v false).
            fe = jnp.where(self.mask.u, fe, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]
            fn = jnp.where(self.mask.v, fn, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]

        out = jnp.zeros_like(h)
        # dh[k, j, i] = -( (fe[k,j,i+1/2] - fe[k,j,i-1/2])/dx
        #                 + (fn[k,j+1/2,i] - fn[k,j-1/2,i])/dy )
        if wall == "open":
            # Overwrite the west/east (fe cols 0, -2) and south/north
            # (fn rows 0, -2) lateral wall faces with a first-order upwind
            # flux that reads the ghost ring, then write the full horizontal
            # interior.  z is a batch dimension and keeps the full [1:-1].
            fe = fe.at[:, :, 0].set(
                _wall_upwind_flux(u[:, :, 0], h[:, :, 0], h[:, :, 1])
            )
            fe = fe.at[:, :, -2].set(
                _wall_upwind_flux(u[:, :, -2], h[:, :, -2], h[:, :, -1])
            )
            fn = fn.at[:, 0, :].set(
                _wall_upwind_flux(v[:, 0, :], h[:, 0, :], h[:, 1, :])
            )
            fn = fn.at[:, -2, :].set(
                _wall_upwind_flux(v[:, -2, :], h[:, -2, :], h[:, -1, :])
            )
            out = out.at[1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1].set(
                -(
                    (fe[1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1] - fe[1:-1, 1:-1, 0:-2]) / self.grid.dx
                    + (fn[1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1] - fn[1:-1, 0:-2, 1:-1]) / self.grid.dy
                )
            )
        else:
            # Reconstruction writes to [1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1]; the west flux at i=0
            # and south flux at j=0 are ghost cells (value 0, not filled).
            # Consistent with 1D/2D operators, skip the ghost-adjacent interior
            # ring in the horizontal plane so we never read ghost flux cells.
            # All z-levels are independent, so z uses the full interior [1:-1].
            out = out.at[1:-1, 2:-2, 2:-2].set(
                -(
                    (fe[1:-1, 2:-2, 2:-2] - fe[1:-1, 2:-2, 1:-3]) / self.grid.dx
                    + (fn[1:-1, 2:-2, 2:-2] - fn[1:-1, 1:-3, 2:-2]) / self.grid.dy
                )
            )
        if self.mask is not None:
            out = jnp.where(self.mask.h, out, 0.0)
        return out

def __call__(
    self,
    h: Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"],
    u: Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"],
    v: Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"],
    method: str = "upwind1",
    wall: str = "closed",
) -> Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]:
    """Advective tendency -div(h * u_vec) at T-points over all z-levels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    h : Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
        Scalar at T-points.
    u : Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
        x-velocity at U-points.
    v : Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
        y-velocity at V-points.
    method : str
        Reconstruction method: ``'naive'``, ``'upwind1'``, ``'weno3'``,
        ``'weno5'``, ``'wenoz5'``, ``'weno7'``, ``'weno9'``, or a
        flux-limiter TVD scheme: ``'minmod'``, ``'van_leer'``,
        ``'superbee'``, ``'mc'``.  (``upwind2`` / ``upwind3`` are 1-D /
        2-D only: :class:`Reconstruction3D` has no such stencils.)
    wall : {"closed", "open"}, default "closed"
        Lateral-boundary treatment for the horizontal plane.
        ``"closed"`` (default, unchanged) writes the horizontal tendency
        only on the strict interior ``[1:-1, 2:-2, 2:-2]`` and treats the
        four lateral walls as no-flux — the wall-adjacent interior ring
        holds stale values.  ``"open"`` writes the full interior
        ``[1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1]`` and computes the lateral domain-wall face
        fluxes with a first-order upwind reconstruction that reads the
        ghost ring, so Dirichlet / outflow / periodic lateral boundaries
        (applied by the caller to the ghost cells beforehand) drive
        horizontal transport.  Interior faces keep the requested
        high-order ``method`` and the flux field stays single-valued, so
        mass is conserved exactly.  The z axis is a batch dimension and is
        unaffected.  ``"open"`` is not supported together with a ``mask``.

    Returns
    -------
    Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
        Advective tendency at T-points.
    """
    _validate_wall(wall, self.mask)
    if self.mask is not None:
        # Zero the dry inputs before any stencil reads them, so land
        # values (even NaN) reach neither the output nor its gradient.
        h = jnp.where(self.mask.h, h, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]
        u = jnp.where(self.mask.u, u, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]
        v = jnp.where(self.mask.v, v, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]
    # ── masked path: route through upwind_flux with pre-built 3-D hier. ──
    mh_x = self._mask_hierarchy_x
    mh_y = self._mask_hierarchy_y
    if mh_x is not None and mh_y is not None and method in _MASK_DISPATCHABLE:
        rfx, rfy, sizes = _rec_funcs_for_method_3d(self.recon, method)
        mask_x = narrow_mask_hierarchy(mh_x, sizes)
        mask_y = narrow_mask_hierarchy(mh_y, sizes)
        # 3-D arrays: x-flux axis is 2, y-flux axis is 1.
        fe = upwind_flux(h, u, dim=2, rec_funcs=rfx, mask_hierarchy=mask_x)
        fn = upwind_flux(h, v, dim=1, rec_funcs=rfy, mask_hierarchy=mask_y)
    # ── unmasked path: existing dispatch ────────────────────────────
    elif method == "naive":
        fe = self.recon.naive_x(h, u)
        fn = self.recon.naive_y(h, v)
    elif method == "upwind1":
        fe = self.recon.upwind1_x(h, u)
        fn = self.recon.upwind1_y(h, v)
    elif method == "weno3":
        fe = self.recon.weno3_x(h, u)
        fn = self.recon.weno3_y(h, v)
    elif method == "weno5":
        fe = self.recon.weno5_x(h, u)
        fn = self.recon.weno5_y(h, v)
    elif method == "wenoz5":
        fe = self.recon.wenoz5_x(h, u)
        fn = self.recon.wenoz5_y(h, v)
    elif method == "weno7":
        fe = self.recon.weno7_x(h, u)
        fn = self.recon.weno7_y(h, v)
    elif method == "weno9":
        fe = self.recon.weno9_x(h, u)
        fn = self.recon.weno9_y(h, v)
    elif method in _TVD_LIMITERS:
        fe = self.recon.tvd_x(h, u, limiter=method)
        fn = self.recon.tvd_y(h, v, limiter=method)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown method: {method!r}")
    if self.mask is not None:
        # No flux through a dry face (mask.u / mask.v false).
        fe = jnp.where(self.mask.u, fe, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]
        fn = jnp.where(self.mask.v, fn, 0.0)  # [Nz, Ny, Nx]

    out = jnp.zeros_like(h)
    # dh[k, j, i] = -( (fe[k,j,i+1/2] - fe[k,j,i-1/2])/dx
    #                 + (fn[k,j+1/2,i] - fn[k,j-1/2,i])/dy )
    if wall == "open":
        # Overwrite the west/east (fe cols 0, -2) and south/north
        # (fn rows 0, -2) lateral wall faces with a first-order upwind
        # flux that reads the ghost ring, then write the full horizontal
        # interior.  z is a batch dimension and keeps the full [1:-1].
        fe = fe.at[:, :, 0].set(
            _wall_upwind_flux(u[:, :, 0], h[:, :, 0], h[:, :, 1])
        )
        fe = fe.at[:, :, -2].set(
            _wall_upwind_flux(u[:, :, -2], h[:, :, -2], h[:, :, -1])
        )
        fn = fn.at[:, 0, :].set(
            _wall_upwind_flux(v[:, 0, :], h[:, 0, :], h[:, 1, :])
        )
        fn = fn.at[:, -2, :].set(
            _wall_upwind_flux(v[:, -2, :], h[:, -2, :], h[:, -1, :])
        )
        out = out.at[1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1].set(
            -(
                (fe[1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1] - fe[1:-1, 1:-1, 0:-2]) / self.grid.dx
                + (fn[1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1] - fn[1:-1, 0:-2, 1:-1]) / self.grid.dy
            )
        )
    else:
        # Reconstruction writes to [1:-1, 1:-1, 1:-1]; the west flux at i=0
        # and south flux at j=0 are ghost cells (value 0, not filled).
        # Consistent with 1D/2D operators, skip the ghost-adjacent interior
        # ring in the horizontal plane so we never read ghost flux cells.
        # All z-levels are independent, so z uses the full interior [1:-1].
        out = out.at[1:-1, 2:-2, 2:-2].set(
            -(
                (fe[1:-1, 2:-2, 2:-2] - fe[1:-1, 2:-2, 1:-3]) / self.grid.dx
                + (fn[1:-1, 2:-2, 2:-2] - fn[1:-1, 1:-3, 2:-2]) / self.grid.dy
            )
        )
    if self.mask is not None:
        out = jnp.where(self.mask.h, out, 0.0)
    return out

docs.text:
Bases: Module

Apply a Dirichlet value on one domain face.

For a cell-centred field (point="T", the default) the value is imposed at the physical wall between the first interior cell and the ghost cell:

phi_boundary = 0.5 * (phi_interior + phi_ghost), i.e. phi_ghost = 2 * value - phi_interior.

For a node on the wall (the normal velocity U on west / east or V on south / north, any X field) the wall node is set to value directly. A closed wall for the normal velocity is therefore Dirichlet1D("east", 0.0, point="U"); without point="U" the east wall face U[:, Nx-2] is left untouched and mass leaks through it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default face Literal['south', 'north', 'west', 'east']

Domain face to update.

required value float

Target boundary value.

required point Literal['T', 'U', 'V', 'X']

C-grid point the field lives on (default "T"). For a node on the wall (U / X on west / east, V / X on south / north) the condition is imposed on the wall node itself (see the module docstring).

required

Examples:

No normal flow through the west and east walls of a U-field:

>>> u = jnp.ones((6, 6))
>>> u = Dirichlet1D("west", 0.0, point="U")(u, dx=1.0, dy=1.0)
>>> u = Dirichlet1D("east", 0.0, point="U")(u, dx=1.0, dy=1.0)
>>> float(u[2, 0]), float(u[2, -2])  # the two wall faces
(0.0, 0.0)

class Dirichlet1D(eqx.Module):
    """Apply a Dirichlet value on one domain face.

    For a cell-centred field (``point="T"``, the default) the value is
    imposed at the physical wall between the first interior cell and the
    ghost cell:

    ``phi_boundary = 0.5 * (phi_interior + phi_ghost)``,
    i.e. ``phi_ghost = 2 * value - phi_interior``.

    For a node on the wall (the normal velocity ``U`` on west / east or
    ``V`` on south / north, any ``X`` field) the wall node is set to
    ``value`` directly.  A closed wall for the normal velocity is therefore
    ``Dirichlet1D("east", 0.0, point="U")``; without ``point="U"`` the east
    wall face ``U[:, Nx-2]`` is left untouched and mass leaks through it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    face : Literal["south", "north", "west", "east"]
        Domain face to update.
    value : float
        Target boundary value.
    point : Literal["T", "U", "V", "X"], optional
        C-grid point the field lives on (default ``"T"``).  For a node on
        the wall (``U`` / ``X`` on west / east, ``V`` / ``X`` on south /
        north) the condition is imposed on the wall node itself (see the
        module docstring).

    Examples
    --------
    No normal flow through the west and east walls of a U-field:

    >>> u = jnp.ones((6, 6))
    >>> u = Dirichlet1D("west", 0.0, point="U")(u, dx=1.0, dy=1.0)
    >>> u = Dirichlet1D("east", 0.0, point="U")(u, dx=1.0, dy=1.0)
    >>> float(u[2, 0]), float(u[2, -2])  # the two wall faces
    (0.0, 0.0)
    """

    face: Face = eqx.field(static=True)
    value: float
    point: Point = eqx.field(static=True, default="T")

    def __call__(
        self, field: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], dx: float, dy: float

class Neumann1D(eqx.Module):
    """Apply an outward-normal gradient on one domain face.

    The gradient is interpreted as ``dphi/dn`` along the outward normal,
    evaluated over the one-cell distance between the first interior node
    and the boundary node: the ghost node for a cell-centred field (the
    difference is centred on the wall face), the wall node itself for a
    node on the wall (a one-sided difference; the outside slot then makes
    the centred difference across the wall node equal ``value`` too).

    Parameters
    ----------
    face : Literal["south", "north", "west", "east"]
        Domain face to update.
    value : float, optional
        Outward-normal gradient. Defaults to ``0.0`` for zero-gradient
        boundaries.
    point : Literal["T", "U", "V", "X"], optional
        C-grid point the field lives on (default ``"T"``).  For a node on
        the wall (``U`` / ``X`` on west / east, ``V`` / ``X`` on south /
        north) the condition is imposed on the wall node itself (see the
        module docstring).
    """

    face: Face = eqx.field(static=True)
    value: float = 0.0
    point: Point = eqx.field(static=True, default="T")

    def __call__(
        self, field: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], dx: float, dy: float
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Return ``field`` with one Neumann ghost face updated."""
        spacing = _normal_spacing(self.face, dx=dx, dy=dy)
        interior = _adjacent_interior(field, self.face, self.point)
        # The boundary node lies one cell outward of the interior on every
        # face, so dphi/dn = (boundary - interior) / spacing
        #   =>  boundary = interior + g * spacing.
        boundary = interior + (self.value * spacing)  # [N]
        return _set_face(field, self.face, boundary, self.point)

Bases: Module

Slip boundary condition for tangential velocity at a solid wall.

Controls the tangential velocity at the wall via a slip coefficient a in [0, 1]:

  • a = 1.0 — free-slip: ghost = +interior (zero gradient, frictionless wall).
  • a = 0.0 — no-slip: ghost = -interior (zero tangential velocity at wall).
  • 0 < a < 1 — partial-slip: linear interpolation between the two.

The ghost cell is set using:

phi_ghost = (2*a - 1) * phi_interior

so that the extrapolated wall value phi_wall = 0.5 * (phi_ghost + phi_interior) = a * phi_interior smoothly varies from zero (no-slip) to the interior value (free-slip). For a node on the wall (e.g. an X-point field) the wall node is set to a * phi_interior directly.

class Slip1D(eqx.Module):
    """Slip boundary condition for tangential velocity at a solid wall.

    Controls the tangential velocity at the wall via a slip coefficient
    ``a in [0, 1]``:

    - ``a = 1.0`` — **free-slip**: ghost = +interior (zero gradient, frictionless wall).
    - ``a = 0.0`` — **no-slip**: ghost = -interior (zero tangential velocity at wall).
    - ``0 < a < 1`` — **partial-slip**: linear interpolation between the two.

    The ghost cell is set using:

    ``phi_ghost = (2*a - 1) * phi_interior``

    so that the extrapolated wall value
    ``phi_wall = 0.5 * (phi_ghost + phi_interior) = a * phi_interior``
    smoothly varies from zero (no-slip) to the interior value (free-slip).
    For a node on the wall (e.g. an ``X``-point field) the wall node is set
    to ``a * phi_interior`` directly.

    Parameters
    ----------
    face : Literal["south", "north", "west", "east"]
        Domain face to update.
    coefficient : float
        Slip parameter ``a`` in ``[0, 1]``. Default is ``1.0`` (free-slip).
    point : Literal["T", "U", "V", "X"], optional
        C-grid point the field lives on (default ``"T"``).  For a node on
        the wall (``U`` / ``X`` on west / east, ``V`` / ``X`` on south /
        north) the condition is imposed on the wall node itself (see the
        module docstring).

    Examples
    --------
    Free-slip on the west wall (tangential velocity preserved):

    >>> bc = Slip1D("west", coefficient=1.0)
    >>> field_out = bc(field, dx=1.0, dy=1.0)

    No-slip on the north wall (tangential velocity -> 0):

    >>> bc = Slip1D("north", coefficient=0.0)
    >>> field_out = bc(field, dx=1.0, dy=1.0)

    Partial-slip on the south wall:

    >>> bc = Slip1D("south", coefficient=0.5)
    >>> field_out = bc(field, dx=1.0, dy=1.0)
    """

    face: Face = eqx.field(static=True)
    coefficient: float = 1.0
    point: Point = eqx.field(static=True, default="T")

    def __check_init__(self) -> None:
        if not 0.0 <= self.coefficient <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError("Slip1D coefficient must lie in [0, 1].")

    def __call__(
        self, field: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], dx: float, dy: float
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Return ``field`` with one slip ghost face updated.

        Parameters
        ----------
        field : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Input array with ghost-cell ring.
        dx : float
            Grid spacing in x (unused, kept for interface consistency).
        dy : float
            Grid spacing in y (unused, kept for interface consistency).

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Field with the ghost face set according to the slip coefficient.
        """
        del dx, dy
        interior = _adjacent_interior(field, self.face, self.point)
        if _on_wall(self.face, self.point):
            # the node is on the wall: phi_wall = a * interior
            wall = self.coefficient * interior  # [N]
            return _set_face(field, self.face, wall, self.point)
        # ghost = (2*a - 1) * interior
        # wall value = 0.5 * (ghost + interior) = a * interior
        ghost = (2.0 * self.coefficient - 1.0) * interior
        return _set_face(field, self.face, ghost)

class BoundaryConditionSet(eqx.Module):
    """Apply a different boundary condition on each domain face.

    The application order is south, north, west, then east, so west/east
    updates overwrite the corner values written by south/north updates.

    Each atom carries its own ``point`` (the C-grid point of the field); the
    ``closed`` / ``open`` constructors pass one ``point`` to all four faces.
    A closed basin for the velocity is ``BoundaryConditionSet.closed(point="U")``
    for ``u`` and ``closed(point="V")`` for ``v``: zero normal velocity on the
    wall faces and no-slip (``ghost = -interior``) on the tangential walls.

    Parameters
    ----------
    south : BoundaryCondition1D | None, optional
        Boundary condition for the south ghost row.
    north : BoundaryCondition1D | None, optional
        Boundary condition for the north ghost row.
    west : BoundaryCondition1D | None, optional
        Boundary condition for the west ghost column.
    east : BoundaryCondition1D | None, optional
        Boundary condition for the east ghost column.
    mask : Mask2D or Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"] or None, optional
        Domain mask.  When provided, solvers can extract it from the
        BCSet instead of requiring a separate ``mask=`` argument.
    """

    south: BoundaryCondition1D | None = None
    north: BoundaryCondition1D | None = None
    west: BoundaryCondition1D | None = None
    east: BoundaryCondition1D | None = None
    mask: Mask2D | Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"] | None = None

    @classmethod
    def periodic(cls) -> BoundaryConditionSet:
        """Return a fully periodic boundary-condition set."""
        return cls(
            south=Periodic1D("south"),
            north=Periodic1D("north"),
            west=Periodic1D("west"),
            east=Periodic1D("east"),
        )

    @classmethod
    def closed(
        cls,
        mask: Mask2D | Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"] | None = None,
        point: Point = "T",
    ) -> BoundaryConditionSet:
        """Return a zero-Dirichlet boundary-condition set on all faces.

        ``point`` is the C-grid point of the field (``"T"``, ``"U"``, ``"V"``
        or ``"X"``); see :class:`Dirichlet1D`.
        """
        return cls(
            south=Dirichlet1D("south", value=0.0, point=point),
            north=Dirichlet1D("north", value=0.0, point=point),
            west=Dirichlet1D("west", value=0.0, point=point),
            east=Dirichlet1D("east", value=0.0, point=point),
            mask=mask,
        )

    @classmethod
    def open(cls, point: Point = "T") -> BoundaryConditionSet:
        """Return a zero-gradient boundary-condition set on all faces.

        ``point`` is the C-grid point of the field; see :class:`Outflow1D`.
        """
        return cls(
            south=Outflow1D("south", point=point),
            north=Outflow1D("north", point=point),
            west=Outflow1D("west", point=point),
            east=Outflow1D("east", point=point),
        )

    def __call__(
        self, field: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], dx: float, dy: float
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Return ``field`` with all configured ghost faces updated.

        Boundary conditions are applied in south, north, west, east order, so
        west/east updates overwrite the corner values written by south/north.
        """
        out = field
        for bc in (self.south, self.north, self.west, self.east):
            if bc is not None:
                out = bc(out, dx=dx, dy=dy)
        return out

    west/east updates overwrite the corner values written by south/north.
    """
    out = field
    for bc in (self.south, self.north, self.west, self.east):
        if bc is not None:
            out = bc(out, dx=dx, dy=dy)
    return out

class FieldBCSet(eqx.Module):
    """Dispatch per-face boundary conditions across multiple fields.

    Parameters
    ----------
    bc_map : dict[str, BoundaryConditionSet]
        Mapping from state-variable name to per-face boundary conditions.
    default : BoundaryConditionSet | None, optional
        Boundary-condition set used when a variable is not present in
        ``bc_map``. If omitted, unmatched state entries are returned unchanged.
    """

    bc_map: dict[str, BoundaryConditionSet]
    default: BoundaryConditionSet | None = None

    def __call__(
        self, state: dict[str, Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]], dx: float, dy: float
    ) -> dict[str, Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]]:
        """Return a new state dictionary with boundary conditions applied."""
        out: dict[str, Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]] = {}
        for name, field in state.items():
            bc = self.bc_map.get(name, self.default)
            out[name] = field if bc is None else bc(field, dx=dx, dy=dy)
        return out

def pad_interior(
    field: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], mode: str = "edge"
) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
    """Extract physical interior and re-pad to original size.

    Strips the ghost-cell ring, then re-pads using the requested mode.
    Useful for enforcing boundary conditions by re-filling the ghost ring.

    Parameters
    ----------
    field : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
        Input array of shape [Ny, Nx].
    mode : str, optional
        Padding mode passed to ``jnp.pad``.  Defaults to ``'edge'``
        (copy nearest interior value into ghost cells).

    Returns
    -------
    Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
        Array of shape [Ny, Nx] with ghost cells re-filled.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
    >>> f = jnp.ones((6, 6))
    >>> pad_interior(f).shape
    (6, 6)
    """
    if mode == "edge":
        # BoundaryConditionSet.open() is zero-gradient and does not use dx/dy.
        return BoundaryConditionSet.open()(field, dx=1.0, dy=1.0)
    interior = field[..., 1:-1, 1:-1]  # shape [Ny-2, Nx-2]
    return jnp.pad(interior, _pad_last2(field.ndim, 1), mode=mode)  # [..., Ny, Nx]

Bases: Module

Spectral Poisson/Helmholtz solver for masked irregular domains.

Solves (∇² − λ) ψ = f on the wet cells of mask with ψ = 0 on the inner boundary (wet cells adjacent to a dry cell) and outside the mask, using the five-point finite-difference Laplacian.

Method (Buzbee, Golub & Nielson 1970, via gaussx)

Let B be the rectangular operator (periodic / Dirichlet / Neumann by base_bc), I the interior cells (wet, not on the inner boundary) and C the inner-boundary cells, which are exactly the cells outside I that the stencil of I reaches. The masked problem is B[I][:, I] ψ_I = f_I. The capacitance method solves it with two fast rectangular solves per call: find y with y[C] = 0 and (B y)_k = f_k for every k ∉ C (point sources on C absorb the constraints, via an |C| × |C| capacitance matrix factorised once at construction). For a singular base (fft/dct with λ = 0) the constant null vector is included in the capacitance system, so the PDE holds exactly in the interior (gh-87).

Construct with :func:build_capacitance_solver.

Attributes:

Name Type Description operator MaskedOperator

B[I][:, I] with its precomputed capacitance factorisation.

interior_indices Int[Array, 'Ni']

Flat (row-major) indices of the interior cells I.

shape tuple[int, int]

Grid shape (Ny, Nx).

dx, dy float

Grid spacings (static; baked into operator).

lambda_ float

Helmholtz parameter (static).

base_bc str

Rectangular base: "fft", "dst" or "dct" (static).

class CapacitanceSolver(eqx.Module):
    """Spectral Poisson/Helmholtz solver for masked irregular domains.

    Solves ``(∇² − λ) ψ = f`` on the wet cells of ``mask`` with ``ψ = 0`` on
    the *inner boundary* (wet cells adjacent to a dry cell) and outside the
    mask, using the five-point finite-difference Laplacian.

    Method (Buzbee, Golub & Nielson 1970, via gaussx)
    --------------------------------------------------
    Let ``B`` be the rectangular operator (periodic / Dirichlet / Neumann by
    ``base_bc``), ``I`` the interior cells (wet, not on the inner boundary)
    and ``C`` the inner-boundary cells, which are exactly the cells outside
    ``I`` that the stencil of ``I`` reaches. The masked problem is
    ``B[I][:, I] ψ_I = f_I``. The capacitance method solves it with two fast
    rectangular solves per call: find ``y`` with ``y[C] = 0`` and
    ``(B y)_k = f_k`` for every ``k ∉ C`` (point sources on ``C`` absorb the
    constraints, via an ``|C| × |C|`` capacitance matrix factorised once at
    construction). For a singular base (``fft``/``dct`` with λ = 0) the
    constant null vector is included in the capacitance system, so the PDE
    holds exactly in the interior (gh-87).

    Construct with :func:`build_capacitance_solver`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    operator : gaussx.MaskedOperator
        ``B[I][:, I]`` with its precomputed capacitance factorisation.
    interior_indices : Int[Array, "Ni"]
        Flat (row-major) indices of the interior cells ``I``.
    shape : tuple[int, int]
        Grid shape ``(Ny, Nx)``.
    dx, dy : float
        Grid spacings (static; baked into ``operator``).
    lambda_ : float
        Helmholtz parameter (static).
    base_bc : str
        Rectangular base: ``"fft"``, ``"dst"`` or ``"dct"`` (static).
    """

    operator: gaussx.MaskedOperator
    interior_indices: Int[Array, " Ni"]
    shape: tuple[int, int] = eqx.field(static=True)
    dx: float = eqx.field(static=True)
    dy: float = eqx.field(static=True)
    lambda_: float = eqx.field(static=True)
    base_bc: str = eqx.field(static=True)

    def __call__(self, rhs: Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]) -> Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]:
        """Solve (∇² − λ)ψ = rhs on the masked domain.

        Parameters
        ----------
        rhs : Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
            Right-hand side on the full rectangular grid. Only the interior
            cells are used; values on the inner boundary and outside the
            mask are ignored.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
            Solution ψ on the full grid: the masked solve on the interior,
            exactly zero on the inner boundary and outside the mask.
        """
        ny, nx = self.shape
        f_interior = rhs.reshape(ny * nx)[self.interior_indices]
        psi_interior = gaussx.solve(self.operator, f_interior)
        psi = jnp.zeros(ny * nx, dtype=psi_interior.dtype)
        return psi.at[self.interior_indices].set(psi_interior).reshape(ny, nx)

docs.text:
Pre-compute the capacitance matrix and return a ready-to-use solver.

The solver's unknowns are every wet cell of mask, with ψ = 0 on the coast ring (the dry cells 4-adjacent to a wet cell) and outside: the same problem method="cg" solves through :func:masked_laplacian on that mask (for ψ with a :class:Mask2D, the wall on the C-grid wall nodes).

The masked operator is the wet sub-block B[W][:, W] of the rectangular five-point operator B = (∇² − λ) (:func:~finitevolx.masked_helmholtz_operator with bc=base_bc), a gaussx.MaskedOperator whose coupling set is the coast ring. This is an offline function: it factorises the N_c × N_c capacitance matrix (N_c = number of coast cells) with N_c rectangular solves. The returned :class:CapacitanceSolver is then two rectangular solves plus an O(N_c²) back-substitution per right-hand side and is JIT-compilable.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask np.ndarray of bool shape (Ny, Nx), or Mask2D

Physical domain mask. True = wet (ocean/fluid), False = dry (land/walls). A :class:Mask2D gives its ψ (X-point) mask xy_corner_strict.

required dx float

Grid spacing in x.

required dy float

Grid spacing in y.

required lambda_ float

Helmholtz parameter λ ≥ 0. Use 0.0 for pure Poisson.

0.0 base_bc ('dst', 'fft', 'dct')

Rectangular base operator: Dirichlet (DST-I, the default: non-singular for every λ ≥ 0), periodic (FFT) or Neumann (DCT-II). The base only enters through cells beyond the array edge, so every base gives the masked_laplacian solution as long as no wet cell touches the array edge (true for any mask with a dry ghost ring); "fft" and "dct" raise when one does. A singular base ("fft" / "dct" at λ = 0) is handled exactly: gaussx borders the capacitance system with the base's null vector.

"dst"

Returns:

Type Description CapacitanceSolver

A callable equinox Module with all precomputed arrays baked in; it returns ψ on the full grid, zero on every dry cell.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For an unknown base_bc, a mask with no wet cells, a mask with no dry cells (nothing to correct: use the rectangular solver), or a "fft" / "dct" base with a wet cell on the array edge.

Examples:

>>> mask = np.zeros((34, 34), dtype=bool)
>>> mask[1:-1, 1:-1] = True
>>> solver = build_capacitance_solver(Mask2D.from_mask(mask), dx, dy, lambda_=4.0)
>>> psi = streamfunction_from_vorticity(
...     zeta, dx, dy, lambda_=4.0, method="capacitance", capacitance_solver=solver
... )

def build_capacitance_solver(
    mask: np.ndarray | Mask2D,
    dx: float,
    dy: float,
    lambda_: float = 0.0,
    base_bc: str = "dst",
) -> CapacitanceSolver:
    """Pre-compute the capacitance matrix and return a ready-to-use solver.

    The solver's unknowns are **every wet cell** of *mask*, with ψ = 0 on the
    coast ring (the dry cells 4-adjacent to a wet cell) and outside: the same
    problem ``method="cg"`` solves through :func:`masked_laplacian` on that
    mask (for ψ with a :class:`Mask2D`, the wall on the C-grid wall nodes).

    The masked operator is the wet sub-block ``B[W][:, W]`` of the
    rectangular five-point operator ``B = (∇² − λ)``
    (:func:`~finitevolx.masked_helmholtz_operator` with ``bc=base_bc``), a
    ``gaussx.MaskedOperator`` whose coupling set is the coast ring.  This is
    an **offline** function: it factorises the ``N_c × N_c`` capacitance
    matrix (``N_c`` = number of coast cells) with ``N_c`` rectangular solves.
    The returned :class:`CapacitanceSolver` is then two rectangular solves
    plus an ``O(N_c²)`` back-substitution per right-hand side and is
    JIT-compilable.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mask : np.ndarray of bool shape (Ny, Nx), or Mask2D
        Physical domain mask.  ``True`` = wet (ocean/fluid), ``False`` = dry
        (land/walls).  A :class:`Mask2D` gives its ψ (X-point) mask
        ``xy_corner_strict``.
    dx : float
        Grid spacing in x.
    dy : float
        Grid spacing in y.
    lambda_ : float
        Helmholtz parameter λ ≥ 0.  Use ``0.0`` for pure Poisson.
    base_bc : {"dst", "fft", "dct"}
        Rectangular base operator: Dirichlet (DST-I, the default:
        non-singular for every λ ≥ 0), periodic (FFT) or Neumann (DCT-II).
        The base only enters through cells beyond the array edge, so every
        base gives the ``masked_laplacian`` solution as long as no wet cell
        touches the array edge (true for any mask with a dry ghost ring);
        ``"fft"`` and ``"dct"`` raise when one does.  A singular base
        (``"fft"`` / ``"dct"`` at λ = 0) is handled exactly: gaussx borders
        the capacitance system with the base's null vector.

    Returns
    -------
    CapacitanceSolver
        A callable equinox Module with all precomputed arrays baked in; it
        returns ψ on the full grid, zero on every dry cell.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For an unknown ``base_bc``, a mask with no wet cells, a mask with
        no dry cells (nothing to correct: use the rectangular solver), or a
        ``"fft"`` / ``"dct"`` base with a wet cell on the array edge.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> mask = np.zeros((34, 34), dtype=bool)
    >>> mask[1:-1, 1:-1] = True
    >>> solver = build_capacitance_solver(Mask2D.from_mask(mask), dx, dy, lambda_=4.0)
    >>> psi = streamfunction_from_vorticity(
    ...     zeta, dx, dy, lambda_=4.0, method="capacitance", capacitance_solver=solver
    ... )
    """
    if base_bc not in ("fft", "dst", "dct"):
        raise ValueError(f"base_bc must be 'fft', 'dst', or 'dct'; got {base_bc!r}")
    if isinstance(mask, Mask2D):
        mask = np.asarray(mask.xy_corner_strict)
    wet = np.asarray(mask) > 0.5  # [Ny, Nx], concrete
    if not wet.any():
        raise ValueError("The mask has no wet (True) cells.")
    if wet.all():
        raise ValueError(
            "The mask has no dry (False) cells, so there is no coast to "
            f"correct for; use solve_helmholtz_{base_bc} directly."
        )
    edge = wet[0].any() | wet[-1].any() | wet[:, 0].any() | wet[:, -1].any()
    if base_bc != "dst" and edge:
        raise ValueError(
            f"base_bc={base_bc!r} reaches beyond the array edge, where "
            "masked_laplacian (method='cg') has psi = 0, but the mask has wet "
            "cells on the edge: use base_bc='dst' or a mask with a dry ring."
        )
    # The wet block of B = (∇² - λ) on the rectangle (the same eigenvalues as
    # the spectral solvers), coupled to the dry cells through the coast ring.
    operator = masked_helmholtz_operator(
        jnp.asarray(wet), dx, dy, lambda_=lambda_, bc=base_bc
    )
    return CapacitanceSolver(
        operator=operator,
        interior_indices=jnp.asarray(np.flatnonzero(wet.ravel())),
        shape=wet.shape,
        dx=float(dx),
        dy=float(dy),
        lambda_=float(lambda_),
        base_bc=base_bc,
    )

Apply the masked discrete Helmholtz operator (∇² − λ)·ψ.

Enforces homogeneous Dirichlet conditions at the mask boundary by zeroing psi outside the mask before applying the 5-point stencil. The output is also zeroed outside the mask.

Neighbours beyond the array edge are zero (dry), so the array edge is a homogeneous Dirichlet boundary one node outside the array, wherever the mask is wet there; nothing wraps around. On an all-ones mask this is the dense Dirichlet 5-point operator that the DST-I solvers invert, so make_spectral_preconditioner(..., bc="dst") matches it exactly on a rectangle; the FFT preconditioner (periodic) is an approximation.

def masked_laplacian(
    psi: Float[Array, "Ny Nx"],
    mask: Float[Array, "Ny Nx"] | Mask2D,
    dx: float,
    dy: float,
    lambda_: float | Array = 0.0,
) -> Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]:
    """Apply the masked discrete Helmholtz operator (∇² − λ)·ψ.

    Enforces homogeneous Dirichlet conditions at the mask boundary by zeroing
    *psi* outside the mask before applying the 5-point stencil.  The output
    is also zeroed outside the mask.

    Neighbours beyond the array edge are zero (dry), so the array edge is a
    homogeneous Dirichlet boundary one node outside the array, wherever the
    mask is wet there; nothing wraps around.  On an all-ones mask this is
    the dense Dirichlet 5-point operator that the DST-I solvers invert, so
    ``make_spectral_preconditioner(..., bc="dst")`` matches it exactly on a
    rectangle; the FFT preconditioner (periodic) is an approximation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    psi : Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
        Field to which the operator is applied.
    mask : Float[Array, "Ny Nx"] or Mask2D
        Binary mask: 1 inside the physical domain, 0 outside (land/exterior).
        When an :class:`Mask2D` is passed, the ``psi`` staggering
        mask is used (all four surrounding h-cells must be wet).
    dx : float
        Grid spacing in x.
    dy : float
        Grid spacing in y.
    lambda_ : float
        Helmholtz parameter.  Default: 0.0 (pure Laplacian).

    Returns
    -------
    Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
        Result of (∇² − λ)·(ψ·mask), zeroed outside the mask.
    """
    if isinstance(mask, Mask2D):
        mask_arr = mask.xy_corner_strict.astype(psi.dtype)
    else:
        mask_arr = mask
    psi_m = psi * mask_arr  # enforce zero outside domain  [Ny, Nx]
    # Zero ring outside the array (Dirichlet, not periodic); pad once and
    # bind each neighbour view once, so the stencil lowers to one fused pass.
    p = jnp.pad(psi_m, 1)  # [Ny+2, Nx+2]
    east = p[1:-1, 2:]  # ψ[j, i+1]  [Ny, Nx]
    west = p[1:-1, :-2]  # ψ[j, i-1]  [Ny, Nx]
    north = p[2:, 1:-1]  # ψ[j+1, i]  [Ny, Nx]
    south = p[:-2, 1:-1]  # ψ[j-1, i]  [Ny, Nx]
    # ∇²ψ[j, i] = (ψ[j, i+1] + ψ[j, i-1] - 2ψ[j, i]) / dx²
    #           + (ψ[j+1, i] + ψ[j-1, i] - 2ψ[j, i]) / dy²
    lap = (east + west - 2.0 * psi_m) / dx**2 + (north + south - 2.0 * psi_m) / dy**2
    return (lap - lambda_ * psi_m) * mask_arr  # [Ny, Nx]

class Coriolis2D(eqx.Module):
    """Coriolis force operator for 2-D Arakawa C-grids.

    Computes the Coriolis tendency for both velocity components in the
    energy-conserving corner-product form (Sadourny 1975):

        du_cor[j, i+1/2] = +1/2 (P[j+1/2, i+1/2] + P[j-1/2, i+1/2])
        dv_cor[j+1/2, i] = -1/2 (Q[j+1/2, i+1/2] + Q[j+1/2, i-1/2])

        P = f_X * avg_x(v),   Q = f_X * avg_y(u)   at X-points,

    with ``f_X`` the 4-point average of the T-point f.  The kinetic-energy
    tendency ``sum(u * du_cor) + sum(v * dv_cor)`` vanishes to round-off for
    any f, including a beta-plane (the f_on_u * V_to_U(v) form used before
    #289 conserves energy only for uniform f).  For uniform f the two forms
    coincide.

    The corner products are formed on the full arrays (X rows / columns
    ``0 .. N-2``), so the first interior row / column reads the south /
    west ghost corners built from the caller's ghost cells.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : CartesianGrid2D
        The underlying 2-D grid.
    mask : Mask2D or None, optional
        Optional land/ocean mask.  When provided, ``u`` / ``v`` are zeroed
        on dry faces with ``jnp.where`` before the stencil (so NaN-filled
        land cannot leak) and the output on dry U / V faces.  Energy is
        still conserved, and for uniform f the result equals the face form
        on the masked velocities.  ``None`` (default) leaves the output
        untouched.

    Notes
    -----
    ``f`` must be filled on the whole array, ghost ring included (e.g. an
    analytic ``f0 + beta * y`` evaluated at every T-point): the corner
    average ``f_X`` on the first / last interior rows reads the ghost rows
    of ``f``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
    >>> from finitevolx import CartesianGrid2D, Coriolis2D
    >>> grid = CartesianGrid2D.from_interior(8, 8, 1.0, 1.0)
    >>> cor = Coriolis2D(grid=grid)
    >>> u = jnp.zeros((grid.Ny, grid.Nx))
    >>> v = jnp.ones((grid.Ny, grid.Nx))
    >>> f = jnp.ones((grid.Ny, grid.Nx))
    >>> du_cor, dv_cor = cor(u, v, f)
    """

    grid: CartesianGrid2D
    mask: Mask2D | None = None

    def __call__(
        self,
        u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        f: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]]:
        """Coriolis tendencies (du_cor, dv_cor).

        du_cor[j, i+1/2] = +avg_y(f_X * avg_x(v))
        dv_cor[j+1/2, i] = -avg_x(f_X * avg_y(u))

        Parameters
        ----------
        u : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points (east faces).
        v : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points (north faces).
        f : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Coriolis parameter at T-points, ghost ring filled.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]]
            ``(du_cor, dv_cor)`` — Coriolis tendencies at U-points and
            V-points respectively, both zero in the ghost ring.  When
            ``self.mask`` is set, dry U / V faces are zero.
        """
        if self.mask is not None:
            # zero dry faces before any stencil reads them (NaN-filled land)
            u = jnp.where(self.mask.u, u, 0.0)
            v = jnp.where(self.mask.v, v, 0.0)
        # f_X[j+1/2, i+1/2] = 1/4 (f[j, i] + f[j+1, i] + f[j, i+1] + f[j+1, i+1])
        #   X rows / cols 0 .. N-2 (the south / west ghost corners included)
        f_x = 0.25 * (
            f[..., :-1, :-1] + f[..., 1:, :-1] + f[..., :-1, 1:] + f[..., 1:, 1:]
        )  # [Ny-1, Nx-1]
        # v_X[j+1/2, i+1/2] = 1/2 (v[j+1/2, i] + v[j+1/2, i+1])
        v_x = 0.5 * (v[..., :-1, :-1] + v[..., :-1, 1:])  # [Ny-1, Nx-1]
        # u_X[j+1/2, i+1/2] = 1/2 (u[j, i+1/2] + u[j+1, i+1/2])
        u_x = 0.5 * (u[..., :-1, :-1] + u[..., 1:, :-1])  # [Ny-1, Nx-1]
        # corner products P = f_X v_X, Q = f_X u_X              [Ny-1, Nx-1]
        p = f_x * v_x
        q = f_x * u_x
        # du_cor[j, i+1/2] = +1/2 (P[j+1/2, i+1/2] + P[j-1/2, i+1/2])  [Ny-2, Nx-2]
        du_cor = interior(0.5 * (p[..., 1:, 1:] + p[..., :-1, 1:]), u)
        # dv_cor[j+1/2, i] = -1/2 (Q[j+1/2, i+1/2] + Q[j+1/2, i-1/2])  [Ny-2, Nx-2]
        dv_cor = interior(-0.5 * (q[..., 1:, 1:] + q[..., 1:, :-1]), v)

        if self.mask is not None:
            du_cor = jnp.where(self.mask.u, du_cor, 0.0)
            dv_cor = jnp.where(self.mask.v, dv_cor, 0.0)

        return du_cor, dv_cor

class Coriolis3D(eqx.Module):
    """Coriolis force operator for 3-D Arakawa C-grids.

    Applies the same horizontal Coriolis stencil as :class:`Coriolis2D`
    independently at each z-level.  The Coriolis parameter f is 2-D
    (depth-independent) and broadcast over all z-levels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : CartesianGrid3D
        The underlying 3-D grid.
    mask : Mask3D or None, optional
        Optional land/ocean mask.  Pattern A (post-compute) — the
        inner :class:`Coriolis2D` is constructed ``mask=None`` and
        the 3-D result is post-multiplied by ``mask.u`` / ``mask.v``
        after the vmap.

        Takes a :class:`Mask3D` (not ``Mask2D``): even though ``f``
        is 2-D and depth-independent, the velocity mask is natively
        3-D on the Arakawa C-grid, and using ``Mask3D`` keeps the
        3-D operator suite type-uniform per #209.  Issue #209's Q4
        locked this in for Advection3D and this commit extends the
        same decision to Coriolis3D.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
    >>> from finitevolx import CartesianGrid3D, Coriolis3D
    >>> grid = CartesianGrid3D.from_interior(6, 6, 4, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    >>> cor = Coriolis3D(grid=grid)
    >>> u = jnp.zeros((grid.Nz, grid.Ny, grid.Nx))
    >>> v = jnp.ones((grid.Nz, grid.Ny, grid.Nx))
    >>> f = jnp.ones((grid.Ny, grid.Nx))
    >>> du_cor, dv_cor = cor(u, v, f)
    """

    grid: CartesianGrid3D
    mask: Mask3D | None
    _cor2d: Coriolis2D

    def __init__(
        self,
        grid: CartesianGrid3D,
        mask: Mask3D | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.grid = grid
        self.mask = mask
        # Pattern A: inner 2-D op is mask-free; the 3-D wrapper owns the mask.
        self._cor2d = Coriolis2D(grid=grid.horizontal_grid())

    def __call__(
        self,
        u: Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"],
        f: Float[Array, "Ny Nx"],
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"], Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]]:
        """Coriolis tendencies over all z-levels.

        du_cor[k, j, i+1/2] = +avg_y(f_X * avg_x(v[k]))
        dv_cor[k, j+1/2, i] = -avg_x(f_X * avg_y(u[k]))

        (the energy-conserving form of :class:`Coriolis2D` at each level)

        Parameters
        ----------
        u : Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.
        f : Float[Array, "Ny Nx"]
            Coriolis parameter at T-points (depth-independent).

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"], Float[Array, "Nz Ny Nx"]]
            ``(du_cor, dv_cor)`` — Coriolis tendencies at U-points and
            V-points, both zero in the ghost ring.  When ``self.mask``
            is set, ``du_cor`` is zeroed at dry U-faces via
            ``* mask.u`` and ``dv_cor`` at dry V-faces via ``* mask.v``.
        """
        if self.mask is not None:
            # zero dry faces before the stencil, as Coriolis2D does
            u = jnp.where(self.mask.u, u, 0.0)
            v = jnp.where(self.mask.v, v, 0.0)
        # Vmap the 2D Coriolis operator over z-levels.
        # f is 2D (depth-independent) and broadcast to each z-slice.
        du_cor, dv_cor = eqx.filter_vmap(lambda u_k, v_k: self._cor2d(u_k, v_k, f))(
            u, v
        )

        # Zero the z-ghost slices to match the 3D ghost-ring convention.
        du_cor = zero_z_ghosts(du_cor)
        dv_cor = zero_z_ghosts(dv_cor)

        if self.mask is not None:
            du_cor = du_cor * self.mask.u
            dv_cor = dv_cor * self.mask.v

        return du_cor, dv_cor

docs.title: Diagnostic Quantities
docs.text:
Pointwise and domain-integrated diagnostic quantities on Arakawa C-grids.

Each diagnostic in the table below comes in two forms:

  • Class operators (Layer 3) take the land/ocean mask at construction and zero the dry cells of their output stagger — use these in masked domains.
  • Functional helpers (Layer 2) are mask-free; apply the mask yourself at the call site if you use them directly.

The domain-integrated total_energy / total_enstrophy and vertical_velocity have no class form: pass the reductions fields that are already masked (e.g. from the class operators), and give vertical_velocity a Mask3D as its per-call mask= argument.

See Masks → Operator API for the stagger → mask mapping.

Diagnostic Class method Functional helper Output Kinetic energy Energetics2D.kinetic_energy kinetic_energy T Bernoulli potential Energetics2D.bernoulli_potential bernoulli_potential T Available potential energy Energetics2D.available_potential_energy available_potential_energy T Relative vorticity Vorticity2D.relative_vorticity relative_vorticity_cgrid X Shallow-water PV Vorticity2D.potential_vorticity sw_potential_vorticity¹ X Enstrophy Vorticity2D.enstrophy enstrophy X Potential enstrophy Vorticity2D.potential_enstrophy potential_enstrophy X Shear strain Strain2D.shear shear_strain X Tensor strain Strain2D.tensor tensor_strain T Strain magnitude² Strain2D.magnitude_squared strain_magnitude_squared T Okubo–Weiss Strain2D.okubo_weiss okubo_weiss T QG PV (one layer) QGPotentialVorticity2D.__call__ qg_potential_vorticity T Stretching term QGPotentialVorticity2D.stretching stretching_term T QG PV (multilayer) QGPotentialVorticity2D.multilayer potential_vorticity_multilayer T

¹ Not identical where the thickness at a corner is zero: sw_potential_vorticity returns 0 there, while Vorticity2D.potential_vorticity returns a NaN sentinel at wet corners (dry corners are exactly 0 under a mask), so a degenerate layer is flagged rather than hidden.

The functional strain_magnitude_squared / okubo_weiss / enstrophy / potential_enstrophy are pointwise: their inputs must already share a grid point. The class methods do the staggering for you — Strain2D averages the X-point shear and vorticity to T-points, Vorticity2D.potential_enstrophy averages h to X-points.

Every method returns a T-point field with a zero ghost ring; when mask is set, inputs are zeroed on dry interior cells first and dry T-cells are zeroed last (via jnp.where(mask.h, ...)); see the module docstring.

>>> grid = CartesianGrid2D.from_interior(8, 8, 1.0, 1.0)

class Energetics2D(eqx.Module):
    """Energy diagnostics at T-points on a 2-D Arakawa C-grid.

    Class form of :func:`~finitevolx.kinetic_energy`,
    :func:`~finitevolx.bernoulli_potential` and
    :func:`~finitevolx.available_potential_energy`.  Every method returns a
    T-point field with a zero ghost ring; when ``mask`` is set, inputs are
    zeroed on dry interior cells first and dry T-cells are zeroed last (via
    ``jnp.where(mask.h, ...)``); see the module docstring.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : CartesianGrid2D
        The underlying 2-D grid.
    mask : Mask2D or None, optional
        Optional land/ocean mask.  ``None`` (default) returns exactly the
        functional forms' output (for :meth:`available_potential_energy`,
        on the interior; see there).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
    >>> from finitevolx import CartesianGrid2D, Energetics2D
    >>> grid = CartesianGrid2D.from_interior(8, 8, 1.0, 1.0)
    >>> u = jnp.ones((grid.Ny, grid.Nx))
    >>> ke = Energetics2D(grid=grid).kinetic_energy(u, 0.0 * u)
    """

    grid: CartesianGrid2D
    mask: Mask2D | None = None

    def _uv(
        self, u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]]:
        """Zero velocities on dry interior faces (no-normal-flow)."""
        if self.mask is None:
            return u, v
        return _sanitize(self.mask.u, u), _sanitize(self.mask.v, v)

    def _t(self, field: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Zero a T-field on dry interior cells."""
        return _sanitize(None if self.mask is None else self.mask.h, field)

    def _out(self, out: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Zero dry T-cells: out[j, i] = out[j, i] if mask.h[j, i] else 0."""
        return _where(None if self.mask is None else self.mask.h, out)

    def kinetic_energy(
        self,
        u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Kinetic energy at T-points.

        ke[j, i] = 1/2 * (u2_on_T[j, i] + v2_on_T[j, i])

        u2_on_T[j, i] = 1/2 * (u[j, i+1/2]^2 + u[j, i-1/2]^2)
        v2_on_T[j, i] = 1/2 * (v[j+1/2, i]^2 + v[j-1/2, i]^2)

        Parameters
        ----------
        u : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Kinetic energy at T-points, zero in the ghost ring and, when
            ``self.mask`` is set, at dry T-cells.
        """
        u, v = self._uv(u, v)
        return self._out(kinetic_energy(u, v))

    def bernoulli_potential(
        self,
        h: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        gravity: float = GRAVITY,
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Bernoulli potential at T-points.

        p[j, i] = ke[j, i] + gravity * h[j, i]

        Parameters
        ----------
        h : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Layer thickness at T-points.
        u : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.
        gravity : float, optional
            Gravitational acceleration.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Bernoulli potential at T-points, zero in the ghost ring and,
            when ``self.mask`` is set, at dry T-cells.
        """
        u, v = self._uv(u, v)
        return self._out(bernoulli_potential(self._t(h), u, v, gravity))

    def available_potential_energy(
        self,
        h: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        H: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        g_prime: float | Float[Array, ""],
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Available potential energy at T-points.

        ape[j, i] = 1/2 * g_prime * (h[j, i] - H[j, i])^2

        The functional form is pointwise over the whole array; the class
        writes only the interior ``[1:-1, 1:-1]`` and leaves the ghost ring
        zero, like every other operator.

        Parameters
        ----------
        h : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Layer thickness at T-points.
        H : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Reference layer thickness at T-points.
        g_prime : float
            Reduced gravity.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Available potential energy at T-points, zero in the ghost ring
            and, when ``self.mask`` is set, at dry T-cells.
        """
        h, H = self._t(h), self._t(H)
        # Evaluate on the interior only, so ghost values never enter the
        # arithmetic (or its gradient):
        # ape[j, i] = 1/2 * g_prime * (h[j, i] - H[j, i])^2
        #             for 1 <= j <= Ny-2, 1 <= i <= Nx-2
        ape = available_potential_energy(
            h[..., 1:-1, 1:-1], H[..., 1:-1, 1:-1], g_prime
        )
        out = jnp.zeros_like(h, dtype=ape.dtype).at[..., 1:-1, 1:-1].set(ape)
        return self._out(out)

class Strain2D(eqx.Module):
    """Strain diagnostics on a 2-D Arakawa C-grid.

    Class form of :func:`~finitevolx.shear_strain`,
    :func:`~finitevolx.tensor_strain`,
    :func:`~finitevolx.strain_magnitude_squared` and
    :func:`~finitevolx.okubo_weiss`.

    The shear strain lives at X-points and the tensor strain at T-points.
    :meth:`magnitude_squared` and :meth:`okubo_weiss` combine them at
    **T-points**: the X-point shear (and vorticity) are averaged to T-points
    with :meth:`Interpolation2D.X_to_T`, which reads the south ghost X-row
    and west ghost X-column.  Those X ghosts are BC-owned but hidden inside
    the method, so they are computed here from the caller's ghost ``u`` and
    ``v`` (see :meth:`magnitude_squared`) -- apply boundary conditions to
    ``u`` and ``v`` before calling.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : CartesianGrid2D
        The underlying 2-D grid.
    mask : Mask2D or None, optional
        Optional land/ocean mask.  Velocities are zeroed on dry faces
        first; each method then zeroes the dry cells of its output stagger
        (``mask.xy_corner_strict`` for :meth:`shear`, ``mask.h``
        otherwise).  For the T-point combinations the X-point intermediates
        are masked before averaging (pass-down, Pattern 2 in
        ``docs/masks.md``), so a coastal T-cell averages in zero from its
        dry corners.  ``None`` (default) returns exactly the functional
        forms' output for :meth:`shear` and :meth:`tensor`.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
    >>> from finitevolx import CartesianGrid2D, Strain2D
    >>> grid = CartesianGrid2D.from_interior(8, 8, 1.0, 1.0)
    >>> u = jnp.ones((grid.Ny, grid.Nx))
    >>> ow = Strain2D(grid=grid).okubo_weiss(u, 0.0 * u)
    """

    grid: CartesianGrid2D
    mask: Mask2D | None
    interp: Interpolation2D

    def __init__(
        self,
        grid: CartesianGrid2D,
        mask: Mask2D | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.grid = grid
        self.mask = mask
        self.interp = Interpolation2D(grid=grid, mask=mask)

    def _uv(
        self, u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"], Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]]:
        """Zero velocities on dry interior faces (no-normal-flow)."""
        if self.mask is None:
            return u, v
        return _sanitize(self.mask.u, u), _sanitize(self.mask.v, v)

    def _x_with_ghosts(
        self,
        u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        sign: float,
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """dv/dx + sign * du/dy at X-points, including the BC-owned ghosts.

        sign = +1 gives the shear strain, sign = -1 the relative vorticity:

        x[j+1/2, i+1/2] = (v[j+1/2, i+1] - v[j+1/2, i]) / dx
                        + sign * (u[j+1, i+1/2] - u[j, i+1/2]) / dy

        written for 0 <= j <= Ny-2, 0 <= i <= Nx-2, i.e. the interior plus
        the south ghost X-row (j = 0) and west ghost X-column (i = 0), which
        read the caller's ghost u / v.  The north / east X-ghosts are
        outside the domain and stay zero.  At interior X-points this is the
        same arithmetic as :func:`~finitevolx.shear_strain` /
        :func:`~finitevolx.relative_vorticity_cgrid`.

        Under a mask only the dry *interior* corners are zeroed: the south /
        west ghost corners are BC-owned and keep the values derived from
        the ghost velocities, even where a closed-basin mask marks them dry.
        """
        # dv_dx[j+1/2, i+1/2] = (v[j+1/2, i+1] - v[j+1/2, i]) / dx
        dv_dx = (v[..., :-1, 1:] - v[..., :-1, :-1]) / self.grid.dx
        # du_dy[j+1/2, i+1/2] = (u[j+1, i+1/2] - u[j, i+1/2]) / dy
        du_dy = (u[..., 1:, :-1] - u[..., :-1, :-1]) / self.grid.dy
        x = dv_dx + sign * du_dy
        # out[j, i] = x[j, i] for 0 <= j <= Ny-2, 0 <= i <= Nx-2
        out = jnp.zeros_like(u, dtype=x.dtype).at[..., :-1, :-1].set(x)
        return _sanitize(None if self.mask is None else self.mask.xy_corner_strict, out)

    def shear(
        self,
        u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Shear strain at X-points.

        ss[j+1/2, i+1/2] = (v[j+1/2, i+1] - v[j+1/2, i]) / dx
                         + (u[j+1, i+1/2] - u[j, i+1/2]) / dy

        Parameters
        ----------
        u : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Shear strain at X-points, zero in the ghost ring and, when
            ``self.mask`` is set, at dry X-corners.
        """
        u, v = self._uv(u, v)
        out = shear_strain(u, v, self.grid.dx, self.grid.dy)
        return _where(None if self.mask is None else self.mask.xy_corner_strict, out)

    def tensor(
        self,
        u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Tensor (normal) strain at T-points.

        sn[j, i] = (u[j, i+1/2] - u[j, i-1/2]) / dx
                 - (v[j+1/2, i] - v[j-1/2, i]) / dy

        Parameters
        ----------
        u : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Tensor strain at T-points, zero in the ghost ring and, when
            ``self.mask`` is set, at dry T-cells.
        """
        u, v = self._uv(u, v)
        out = tensor_strain(u, v, self.grid.dx, self.grid.dy)
        return _where(None if self.mask is None else self.mask.h, out)

    def magnitude_squared(
        self,
        u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Squared strain magnitude at T-points.

        sigma2[j, i] = sn[j, i]^2 + ss_on_T[j, i]^2

        ss_on_T[j, i] = 1/4 * (ss[j+1/2, i+1/2] + ss[j-1/2, i+1/2]
                             + ss[j+1/2, i-1/2] + ss[j-1/2, i-1/2])

        The first interior row and column read the south / west ghost
        X-points ``ss[1/2, *]`` and ``ss[*, 1/2]``; those are computed from
        the caller's ghost ``u`` / ``v``, so they carry whatever boundary
        condition was applied to the velocities.

        Parameters
        ----------
        u : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Squared strain magnitude at T-points, zero in the ghost ring
            and, when ``self.mask`` is set, at dry T-cells.
        """
        u, v = self._uv(u, v)
        sn = tensor_strain(u, v, self.grid.dx, self.grid.dy)
        ss_on_T = self.interp.X_to_T(self._x_with_ghosts(u, v, 1.0))
        out = strain_magnitude_squared(sn, ss_on_T)
        return _where(None if self.mask is None else self.mask.h, out)

    def okubo_weiss(
        self,
        u: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
        v: Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"],
    ) -> Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]:
        """Okubo-Weiss parameter at T-points.

        ow[j, i] = sn[j, i]^2 + ss_on_T[j, i]^2 - omega_on_T[j, i]^2

        where the X-point shear strain and relative vorticity

        omega[j+1/2, i+1/2] = (v[j+1/2, i+1] - v[j+1/2, i]) / dx
                            - (u[j+1, i+1/2] - u[j, i+1/2]) / dy

        are averaged to T-points over their four surrounding corners
        (including the south / west ghost corners), as in
        :meth:`magnitude_squared`.  Positive = strain-dominated, negative =
        vorticity-dominated.

        Parameters
        ----------
        u : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            x-velocity at U-points.
        v : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            y-velocity at V-points.

        Returns
        -------
        Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
            Okubo-Weiss parameter at T-points, zero in the ghost ring and,
            when ``self.mask`` is set, at dry T-cells.
        """
        u, v = self._uv(u, v)
        sn = tensor_strain(u, v, self.grid.dx, self.grid.dy)
        ss_on_T = self.interp.X_to_T(self._x_with_ghosts(u, v, 1.0))
        omega_on_T = self.interp.X_to_T(self._x_with_ghosts(u, v, -1.0))
        out = okubo_weiss(sn, ss_on_T, omega_on_T)
        return _where(None if self.mask is None else self.mask.h, out)

    Parameters
    ----------
    u : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
        x-velocity at U-points.
    v : Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
        y-velocity at V-points.

    Returns
    -------
    Float[Array, "*batch Ny Nx"]
        Squared strain magnitude at T-points, zero in the ghost ring
        and, when ``self.mask`` is set, at dry T-cells.
    """
    u, v = self._uv(u, v)
    sn = tensor_strain(u, v, self.grid.dx, self.grid.dy)
    ss_on_T = self.interp.X_to_T(self._x_with_ghosts(u, v, 1.0))
    out = strain_magnitude_squared(sn, ss_on_T)
    return _where(None if self.mask is None else self.mask.h, out)
